monthly_review.summary: This month shows clear aerobic progression: faster pace, higher zone 3–4 distribution, and improved VO2max, but at the cost of reduced running economy and rising aerobic TE — likely due to accumulated fatigue masked by strong HRV.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite running 9.4 km less and 4 fewer sessions than last month, average pace improved by 20 sec/km — a meaningful aerobic efficiency gain confirmed by VO2max rising from 36.0 to 39.0, but this is offset by a 3.3% decline in running economy (262.2 vs rolling median 253.9 ml O2/kg/km).

goal_tracker.message: You need 9.4 km across ~4 more runs in 12 days to match last month’s volume — but given chronic sleep debt (4.7h avg, 15/14 days <7h) and declining running economy, chasing that number risks reinforcing inefficient movement patterns; focus instead on quality over quantity and protect sleep first.

insights.title: Chronic sleep deficit correlates with worsening running economy
insights.body: Sleep average is 4.7h (15/14 days <7h), and running economy has deteriorated to 262.2 ml O2/kg/km — the highest (worst) value in the recent 6-run series — while the rolling median is 253.9. This 3.3% drop aligns temporally with the lowest sleep averages observed in May–July.

insights.title: Pace improvement despite rising aerobic TE suggests compensatory effort
insights.body: Avg pace improved (-20 sec/km) while aerobic TE rose (+0.3) and cadence fell (-4 spm), indicating increased physiological cost per unit speed — likely due to fatigue-induced gait inefficiency, not improved fitness.

insights.title: Strong HRV masks underlying recovery debt
insights.body: HRV is +5.7% above baseline and Body Battery +19.3%, yet resting HR dropped only modestly (-1.6 bpm) and training readiness remains low (latest = 46, 7-day avg = 35.8), suggesting autonomic resilience is decoupled from systemic recovery — likely because sleep deprivation impairs CNS restoration independently of HRV.

insights.title: Zone 3–4 volume surged while zone 1 collapsed
insights.body: Zone 3+ share jumped from 47% (May) to 53% (July), driven by 27% Z3 and 19% Z4 — but Z1 dropped from 36% (May) to 14% (July), eroding foundational aerobic stimulus and potentially contributing to elevated aerobic TE and decoupling instability (median recent decoupling = 6.66%, >5% threshold).

recommendations.action: Perform 3x 45-min Zone 1 runs (HR ≤125 bpm, pace ≥9:30 min/km) on Mon/Wed/Fri, no exceptions — even if walking is needed to stay in zone.
recommendations.reason: Z1 volume has collapsed (14% this month vs 36% in May); rebuilding low-intensity aerobic base will lower aerobic TE, improve running economy, and reduce decoupling without taxing recovery.

recommendations.action: Implement strict sleep hygiene: lights out by 22:00, zero screens after 21:30, and 30-min pre-sleep wind-down — target ≥6.5h nightly for next 7 days.
recommendations.reason: Chronic sleep debt (4.7h avg, 15/14 days <7h) is the dominant driver of declining running economy and inefficient gait; HRV gains cannot compensate for CNS fatigue.

recommendations.action: Skip all Zone 4+ efforts for 7 days; replace planned intervals with strides (4x15-sec light accelerations post-Z1 run) only if HRV remains ≥61 ms and sleep ≥6h the prior night.
recommendations.reason: VO2max is stable (39.0), but aerobic decoupling median is 6.66% and recent efficiency is worst in 6 runs — high-intensity work would reinforce inefficient neuromuscular patterning under fatigue.

risk_flags.risk: Gait inefficiency and injury risk from chronic sleep debt
risk_flags.evidence: Sleep avg 4.7h (15/14 days <7h), vertical oscillation rising (7.6→8.5), ground contact time unstable (300–322 ms), and running economy worst in 6-run series (262.2)
risk_flags.action: Prioritize sleep hygiene and eliminate all Z4+ efforts until sleep ≥6.5h avg for 5 consecutive nights.

risk_flags.evidence: Median recent aerobic decoupling = 6.66%, latest = 0.84% (an outlier), but 4 of last 6 runs >6% — including 11.2% and 11.93% — signaling progressive aerobic fatigue.
risk_flags.action: Replace Z3/Z4 runs with Z1 until median decoupling falls below 5% for 3 consecutive runs.

weekly_focus.description: Shift emphasis from pace and volume to neurological restoration and metabolic efficiency — using low-heart-rate running and non-negotiable sleep to reverse gait inefficiency and stabilize decoupling.
